title: Completion of a finite algebra at the primes over a prime
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $\varphi:R\to S$ a ring map making $S$ a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime ideal and let $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_m$ be the prime ideals $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$ (there are finitely many). Let $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nR_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p^nR_{\mathfrak p}$ and $(S_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nS_{\mathfrak q_i}/\mathfrak q_i^nS_{\mathfrak q_i}$ be the completions of these local rings [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] at their maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then there is an isomorphism of $S$-algebras $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i=1}^m(S_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge$ (the right side being the zero ring if $m=0$), compatible with the $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$-algebra structures, where $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ maps to $(S_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge$ by the map induced by the local homomorphism $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q_i}$; both rings are also isomorphic to the $\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak p}$-adic completion of $S_{\mathfrak p}=S\otimes_RR_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension, line 23135) and its proof (Lemmas 0394 finite-after-completion, integral-going-up, artinian-finite-length, 00MA completion-tensor; finitely many primes over p: Lemma 05DR finite-finite-fibres)

proof.text: (Reduction to the local case.) Put $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$ and $B=S\otimes_RR_{\mathfrak p}=S_{\mathfrak p}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] (with $M=R\setminus\mathfrak p$, $D=S$) the map $\lambda:S\to B$, $s\mapsto s\otimes1$, is a localization of $S$ at $W=\varphi(R\setminus\mathfrak p)$. $A$ is a Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module (the $s_j\otimes1$ generate it if the $s_j$ generate $S$ over $R$). Since $S$ is a finite, hence finite type, $R$-algebra, $S$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] (1) for $\lambda$, $\mathfrak Q'\mapsto\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak Q')$ is a bijection from the primes of $B$ onto the primes $\mathfrak Q$ of $S$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)\cap(R\setminus\mathfrak p)=\emptyset$, inverse $\mathfrak Q\mapsto\mathfrak QB$; and (same lemma for $R\to A$) a prime of $A$ equals $\mathfrak m$ iff its preimage in $R$ is $\mathfrak p$. The preimage in $R$ of $\mathfrak Q'$ (via $R\to A\to B$, which equals $R\to S\to B$) is $\varphi^{-1}(\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak Q'))$; hence the primes of $B$ lying over $\mathfrak m$ are exactly the $\mathfrak n_i=\mathfrak q_iB$, $i=1,\dots,m$, pairwise distinct. By part (2) of the same lemma the map $S_{\mathfrak q_i}\to B_{\mathfrak n_i}$, $s/t\mapsto\lambda(s)/\lambda(t)$, is an isomorphism of $S$-algebras; it is compatible with the maps from $A$ (on $A$ both are $a/u\mapsto\varphi(a)/\varphi(u)$) and so carries $\mathfrak m^nS_{\mathfrak q_i}=\mathfrak p^nS_{\mathfrak q_i}$ onto $\mathfrak m^nB_{\mathfrak n_i}$. Finally $S_{\mathfrak q_i}$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. (Stacks: 'we may replace $R$ by $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $S$ by $S_{\mathfrak p}$'.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension, line 23135), first two sentences; Lemma Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization, line 2088); Lemma Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization)

proof.text: (The rings $B/\mathfrak m^nB$.) Fix $n\ge1$ and put $B_n=B/\mathfrak m^nB$, a finite algebra over $A/\mathfrak m^n$. The local ring $A/\mathfrak m^n$ has $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^n$ as its only prime (a prime containing $\mathfrak m^n$ contains $\mathfrak m$, which is maximal). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum], $B_n$ has finitely many primes, each maximal, and their intersection consists of nilpotent elements. The primes of $B_n$ are the $\mathfrak P/\mathfrak m^nB$ with $\mathfrak P\supseteq\mathfrak m^nB$ a prime of $B$; the preimage of such $\mathfrak P$ in $A$ is a proper ideal containing $\mathfrak m^n$, hence equal to $\mathfrak m$, so $\mathfrak P$ is one of the $\mathfrak n_i$ of step 1; conversely $\mathfrak n_i\supseteq\mathfrak mB\supseteq\mathfrak m^nB$. Hence the primes of $B_n$ are exactly the $m$ distinct maximal ideals $\bar{\mathfrak n}_i=\mathfrak n_i/\mathfrak m^nB$ (for $n=1$ this shows that there are finitely many $\mathfrak q_i$, as the statement asserts), and every element of their intersection, the Jacobson radical of $B_n$, is nilpotent. By [lem-weil-pbc-product-of-localizations-at-maximal] the canonical map $B_n\to\prod_{i=1}^m(B_n)_{\bar{\mathfrak n}_i}$ is an isomorphism of $B$-algebras (for $m=0$: $B_n=0$). (Stacks: 'prime ideals of $S/\mathfrak m^nS$ are in 1-to-1 correspondence with $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_m$ ... hence $S/\mathfrak m^nS=\prod S_{\mathfrak q_i}/\mathfrak m^nS_{\mathfrak q_i}$ by 00JB'; the Artinian property used there is replaced by the hypotheses of 00JA checked directly.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension, line 23135), sentences 4-5; Lemma Tag 00JA (lemma-product-local, line 12758), Lemma Tag 06RS proof

proof.text: (Identifying the factors and passing to the limit.) By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] (ring $B$, ideal $\mathfrak m^nB$, prime $\bar{\mathfrak n}_i$) there is a ring isomorphism $(B_n)_{\bar{\mathfrak n}_i}\cong B_{\mathfrak n_i}/\mathfrak m^nB_{\mathfrak n_i}$, $\overline{b}/\overline{t}\leftrightarrow\overline{b/t}$, and by step 1 $B_{\mathfrak n_i}/\mathfrak m^nB_{\mathfrak n_i}\cong S_{\mathfrak q_i}/\mathfrak p^nS_{\mathfrak q_i}$; with step 2 we get isomorphisms of $B$-algebras $\beta_n:B/\mathfrak m^nB\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i=1}^mS_{\mathfrak q_i}/\mathfrak p^nS_{\mathfrak q_i}$ whose $i$-th component is induced by the canonical map $B\to B_{\mathfrak n_i}\cong S_{\mathfrak q_i}$. Since all maps are induced by maps of $B$, the $\beta_n$ commute with the reductions $(\,)/\mathfrak m^{n+1}\to(\,)/\mathfrak m^n$. An inverse limit of a finite product of inverse systems is the product of the inverse limits (compatible sequences are taken componentwise), so the $\beta_n$ give a ring isomorphism of $B$-algebras $\beta:B^\wedge=\varprojlim_nB/\mathfrak m^nB\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i=1}^m\varprojlim_nS_{\mathfrak q_i}/\mathfrak p^nS_{\mathfrak q_i}$, $(x_n)_n\mapsto(\beta_n(x_n))_n$, where $B^\wedge$ is the $\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak p}$-adic ($=\mathfrak mB$-adic) completion of $S_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. It is also $A^\wedge$-linear for the componentwise actions $(a_n)_n\cdot(x_n)_n=(a_nx_n)_n$, $A^\wedge=\varprojlim A/\mathfrak m^n=(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$. (Stacks: 'Hence the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion $S^\wedge$ of $S$ is equal to $\prod S^\wedge_{\mathfrak q_i}$'.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension, line 23135), sentence 6; Proposition Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient, line 1380)

proof.text: (The $\mathfrak p$-adic and $\mathfrak q_i$-adic completions of $S_{\mathfrak q_i}$ agree.) Fix $i$. The map $A\to S_{\mathfrak q_i}$, $a/u\mapsto\varphi(a)/\varphi(u)$, is a local homomorphism (as $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_i)=\mathfrak p$); $\mathfrak m$ and $\mathfrak q_iS_{\mathfrak q_i}$ are finitely generated since $A$ and $S_{\mathfrak q_i}$ are Noetherian (step 1). By step 3 with $n=1$, $S_{\mathfrak q_i}/\mathfrak mS_{\mathfrak q_i}$ is isomorphic, compatibly with the maps from $B$, to the $i$-th factor of $B/\mathfrak mB$, hence is a quotient of the $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$-vector space $B/\mathfrak mB$, which is finite-dimensional because $B$ is a finite $A$-module; so $\dim_\kappa S_{\mathfrak q_i}/\mathfrak mS_{\mathfrak q_i}<\infty$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-after-completion] (1) the map $\gamma_i:\varprojlim_nS_{\mathfrak q_i}/\mathfrak m^nS_{\mathfrak q_i}\to(S_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nS_{\mathfrak q_i}/\mathfrak q_i^nS_{\mathfrak q_i}$ induced by the quotient maps is a ring isomorphism; it is a map of $S_{\mathfrak q_i}$-algebras, and of $A^\wedge$-algebras when $A^\wedge$ acts on the target through the map $\varphi^\wedge$ of that lemma (which is the map induced by $A\to S_{\mathfrak q_i}$), since both are defined componentwise. Hence $\gamma\circ\beta:B^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i=1}^m(S_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge$, $\gamma=\prod_i\gamma_i$, is an isomorphism of $S$-algebras and of $A^\wedge$-algebras. (Stacks: 'The $\mathfrak q_iS_{\mathfrak q_i}$-adic completion $S^\wedge_{\mathfrak q_i}$ is equal to the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion by Lemma 0394'.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension, line 23135), sentence 3; Lemma Tag 0394 (lemma-finite-after-completion, line 23100)

proof.text: (Tensor product description.) $B$ is a finitely generated module over the Noetherian ring $A$ (step 1), so by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] (2) (with $I=\mathfrak m$, $P=B$; note $\mathfrak m^nB$ is the submodule $I^nP$) the $A^\wedge$-linear map $c_B:A^\wedge\otimes_AB\to B^\wedge$, $a\otimes b\mapsto a\cdot\iota_B(b)$, is bijective. It is multiplicative on pure tensors, $c_B((a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b'))=aa'\iota_B(bb')=c_B(a\otimes b)c_B(a'\otimes b')$, because $\iota_B$ is a ring map and $A^\wedge$ acts componentwise; so $c_B$ is an isomorphism of $A^\wedge$-algebras and of $B$-algebras (hence $S$-algebras). By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] (with $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$, the $R$-algebra $S$ and the $R_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra $A^\wedge$) $A^\wedge\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}(R_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_RS)\cong A^\wedge\otimes_RS$, $a\otimes(r\otimes s)\mapsto ra\otimes s$, an isomorphism of $A^\wedge$-algebras which is visibly $S$-linear; with $R_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_RS\cong S\otimes_RR_{\mathfrak p}=B$ (swap of factors) this gives $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RS\cong A^\wedge\otimes_AB\xrightarrow{c_B}B^\wedge$, isomorphisms of $S$-algebras and $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$-algebras. (Stacks: 'Finally, we have $R^\wedge\otimes_RS=S^\wedge$ by Lemma 00MA'.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension, line 23135), last sentence; Lemma Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor, line 22901) part (3)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) Composing step 5 with step 4 gives the isomorphism of $S$-algebras $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\sim}B^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i=1}^m(S_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge$, compatible with the $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$-algebra structures, the $i$-th component of $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\to\prod_i(S_{\mathfrak q_i})^\wedge$ being the map induced by $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q_i}$ (step 4); both rings are isomorphic to the $\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak p}$-adic completion $B^\wedge$ of $S_{\mathfrak p}$. If $m=0$, $B^\wedge=0$ by step 3 and the product is the zero ring.

Proof written in 6 steps after the Stacks proof: (1) reduction to A=R_p, B=S_p via existing nodes (00DK localization-base-change, 00E3-type correspondence lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso, 00FN localization-noetherian, finite-type-algebra-noetherian), identifying the primes of B over pR_p with q_iB and B_{q_iB}=S_{q_i}; (2) B/m^nB has exactly the primes q_iB/m^nB, all maximal, with nil Jacobson radical (existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum, Stacks 06RS proof) so it is the product of its localizations (existing leaf 00JA lem-weil-pbc-product-of-localizations-at-maximal) - this replaces the source's going-up + Artinian (00GU, 00KJ, 00JB) argument by the same facts in the form the DAG has them, and also proves the finiteness of the q_i (05DR not needed); (3) factors identified by 00CT (localization-at-prime-of-quotient) and limits taken (finite products commute with limits, elementary); (4) m-adic = q_i-adic completion of S_{q_i} by lem-weil-pbc-finite-after-completion (0394), hypotheses checked; (5) R_p^ (x)_R S = S_p^ by the 00MA leaf lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor and tensor-cancel-base-change; (6) conclusion, m=0 case. No new nodes. Tags 07N9, 0394, 00MA, 00JA, 00CT, 00DK, 00E3, 06RS verified in tags/tags.
